correctness.rationale: For W5=K1 join C4, invariant spectral sectors have active eigenvalues -2,0,lambda± with lambda±=(q+2±sqrt((q-2)^2+16))/2 and the 2-by-2 symmetric block [[2,2],[2,q]]. Antipodal transfer requires phases at -2 and both lambda± equal -1 while zero mode equals +1. PST would have t=s pi/2 with s odd and u±=s lambda±/2 odd, giving (u+-s)(u--s)=-s^2; LHS is divisible by 4, RHS odd, impossible. For transcendental q, 1,lambda+/4,lambda-/4 are Q-independent; odd Kronecker orbit is dense and supplies PGST. For rational q, PGST requires odd denominator of reduced (q+2)/4 and irrational sqrt((q-2)^2+16), and a one-frequency odd rotation proves both sufficient. Checked characteristic block and q=-2/q=0 examples exactly; irrational algebraic q not classified.

originality.rationale: The all-real hub-only PST obstruction and explicit rational/transcendental PGST boundary do not follow directly from Kempton–Lippner–Yau’s unrestricted vertex-potential existence theorem (its hypotheses and allowed controls differ). Coutinho et al provide general Kronecker/splitting-field tools for integral Hamiltonians, which may decide individual rational q after denominator clearing but do not state this uniform one-control family criterion or transcendental clause. No same W5 hub-only statement found in checked targeted results.
